correctness.rationale: For A equal to a product of elliptic curves, H=sum F_i is principal. D=2F_1 and 2H-D are nonnegative sums of pullbacks of degree-one divisors, hence nef. On the first-factor curve C_1, (H-D).C_1=-1, so H-D is not nef. The standard line-bundle equivalence GV iff nef converts these numerical facts exactly into the asserted generic-vanishing counterexample. All quantifiers and the restriction g>=2 are explicit.

value.rationale: The example tests the exact natural weakening of the new theorem: IT is the strong generic-vanishing condition for line bundles and GV is its boundary analogue. Showing that the implication fails already on product ppav's prevents a tempting but false strengthening and identifies the ampleness boundary geometrically. The family works in every dimension g>=2 and is not an arbitrary numerical slice; it directly targets the theorem's hypothesis.
